page: Amazon Web Services i4g.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 (ARMv8) design running at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 937 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance for compute and memory bandwidth under specific conditions. The stress-ng single-core score of 1520.08 and multi-core score of 6056.47 fall within the average range. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 71.67 GB/sec and write speeds of 34.86 GB/sec, both registering as average. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in other areas, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 969.0 and a multi-core score of 3224.0. Cryptographic and text processing capabilities are limited, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 541.67 and a text processing score of 1188.0, both categorized as poor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i4g.xlarge offers a balanced resource density for storage-heavy workloads by bundling a substantial 937 GB NVMe SSD with an energy-efficient ARM-based processor. While its raw computational and memory bandwidth benchmarks are modest, the high local storage capacity relative to the 4 vCPUs makes it a viable option for localized database operations, caching layers, and storage-intensive applications that do not require intensive floating-point or cryptographic calculations.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.xlarge is a storage-optimized, arm64-based instance powered by 4 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 32.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD, operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks show average results for stress-ng CPU tests and large-block memory bandwidth, though single-core Geekbench and Passmark encryption scores are weak to poor. Qualitatively, the instance provides high storage density relative to its compute resources, making it a cost-efficient choice for storage-intensive workloads. It is best suited for localized databases, caching systems, and general storage-focused applications that benefit from local NVMe SSD performance without requiring high-performance cryptographic or vector processing capabilities.
